title: CX-MT041-AppServerClientCore
clause: Supervised `codex app-server` child + JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio JSONL client core with typed bindings and health probe

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the persistent-lane transport core for the Codex adapter: spawn `codex app-server` as a supervised child process and speak JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio JSONL to it, with request/response correlation, notification dispatch, initialize handshake, typed error mapping, a health probe for the session supervisor, and hand-authored typed bindings for the method/param/result subset Handshake uses. `codex app-server` is the JSON-RPC 2.0 server that powers the official VS Code extension (successor of the deprecated `codex proto`); its primitives are Thread -> Turn -> Item. This MT delivers ONLY the client/transport core; thread lifecycle mapping is MT-042, turn/steer/interrupt is MT-043, approvals are MT-044.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module directory src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/codex_app_server/ containing mod.rs (module root + re-exports), client.rs (AppServerClient: spawn, handshake, request/response correlation, notification dispatch, shutdown), protocol.rs (JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope types + hand-authored typed bindings for the used method set), error.rs (CodexAppServerError), health.rs (health probe + liveness snapshot). One `pub mod codex_app_server;` registration line (plus minimal re-exports) in src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/mod.rs. A minimal visibility change in official_cli_bridge.rs is permitted ONLY to reuse the existing Windows npm-shim resolution + identity verification (e.g. widen `resolve_codex_npm_shim` / the launch-plan identity helpers to pub(crate) behind their existing contract); NO behavior change to the exec lane.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. SPAWN + WINDOWS SHIM REUSE. The child argv is `codex app-server` (no --json; app-server speaks JSON-RPC on stdio by default; stdio JSONL is the stable transport - the WebSocket transport is experimental and REJECTED for this WP; do not implement it). On Windows the configured executable is the npm shim `codex.cmd`; the adapter MUST NOT launch it through cmd.exe. Reuse the exec lane's resolution: official_cli_bridge.rs `resolve_codex_npm_shim` (line 1263) verifies the shim body references node_modules\@openai\codex\bin\codex.js, verifies the launcher package manifest identity (name == "@openai/codex", bin.codex == "bin/codex.js", lines 1317-1332), resolves node.exe (local-to-shim first, then PATH, lines 1306-1312), and yields a pinned final native executable that is executed DIRECTLY so Node never sits in the runtime process tree (see cli_launch_plan lines 1223-1240). The app-server spawn must go through the same identity-locked plan. Child processes are registered with the MT-005 session supervisor seam (ownership metadata owner_session/owner_wp/owner_role/started_at; kill-on-drop; reclamation at session close/failure/staleness per HBR-QUIET-003) and use the MT-004 stdio infrastructure for non-blocking reads/writes.
2. JSON-RPC 2.0 FRAMING. Transport is newline-delimited JSON (one JSON-RPC message per line) on the child's stdin/stdout. Reuse the incremental UTF-8 decode + line-split discipline of cli_bridge_runtime.rs (line accumulator around line 152) including a hard cap on a single unterminated line (cap constant near cli_bridge_runtime.rs line 64) so a misbehaving server cannot balloon memory. stderr is drained to a bounded ring buffer and surfaced in error context.
3. CORRELATION. Outgoing requests carry a process-monotonic u64 id (AtomicU64). A correlation map (Mutex<HashMap<u64, oneshot::Sender<Result<serde_json::Value, JsonRpcErrorObject>>>>) resolves responses to callers. Per-request timeout (default 60s, configurable) fails the oneshot with CodexAppServerError::Timeout. When the child exits or the read loop ends, ALL pending entries are drained with CodexAppServerError::ChannelClosed - no caller may hang forever.
4. NOTIFICATION DISPATCH. Server-to-client messages WITHOUT an id are notifications (thread/turn/item event stream); messages WITH an id and a method are server-to-client REQUESTS (approval requests - MT-044 consumes these; this MT must route them to a registered handler slot and, when no handler is registered, respond with a typed JSON-RPC error rather than dropping the id). Notifications fan out over a bounded tokio broadcast/mpsc channel; overflow is recorded (dropped-count) and never blocks the read loop.
5. INITIALIZE HANDSHAKE. On spawn, the client performs the app-server initialize exchange (send the initialize request with client identity, await the server response, then send the initialized notification) before any other method is permitted; a handshake timeout (default 30s) is a typed CodexAppServerError::Handshake. NOTE: exact method/field casing MUST be taken from the typed schema exported by `codex app-server generate-json-schema` (or `generate-ts`) at implementation time - that export is the schema source of truth for the bindings in protocol.rs; record the CLI version the bindings were authored against in a const (BINDINGS_AUTHORED_AGAINST_CODEX_VERSION) that MT-047's drift check consumes.
6. TYPED BINDINGS (protocol.rs). Hand-authored serde structs/enums for exactly the subset Handshake uses: JSON-RPC envelope (JsonRpcRequest/JsonRpcResponse/JsonRpcNotification/JsonRpcErrorObject with code/message/data), initialize params/result, thread/start, thread/resume, thread/fork, thread/list, thread/read, thread/rollback, turn/start, turn/steer, turn/interrupt params/results, the approval request payloads item/commandExecution/requestApproval + item/fileChange/requestApproval, and event notifications thread.started, turn.started, turn.completed (with token usage), turn.failed if present in the schema, item.started/item.updated/item.completed with item types agent_message, reasoning, command_execution, file_change, mcp_tool_call, web_search, plan_update. All event enums carry a lossless Unknown{raw} variant so schema additions never panic the adapter.
7. TYPED ERRORS (error.rs). enum CodexAppServerError { SpawnFailed, ShimIdentity, Handshake, Transport, Protocol(JsonRpcErrorObject), Timeout, ChannelClosed, Shutdown, Unsupported }. Every public API returns Result<_, CodexAppServerError>; no stringly-typed errors on the public surface.
8. HEALTH PROBE (health.rs). health() returns a typed snapshot: child pid + alive?, handshake completed?, last_rx_at/last_tx_at instants, pending request count, dropped notification count, and a round-trip probe using the cheapest schema-available method (thread/list with a small page). The MT-005 supervisor consumes this for restart/circuit-breaker policy; this MT only exposes the probe, it does not implement restart policy.
9. SHUTDOWN. Graceful: close stdin, await child exit with bounded deadline, then kill. Drop = kill-on-drop. No orphan `codex app-server` processes after any test run.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the MT-004 stdio infrastructure and MT-005 supervisor seam contracts and their delivered code in the implementation worktree; read official_cli_bridge.rs lines 963-1015 (validate_cli_preset), 1160-1249 (launch plan), 1263 onward (resolve_codex_npm_shim) and cli_bridge_runtime.rs (line accumulator + cap) before writing code.
2. Create codex_app_server/mod.rs with module docs stating: stdio JSONL = stable transport; WebSocket = experimental, REJECTED; schema source of truth = `codex app-server generate-json-schema`.
3. Author protocol.rs envelope + typed bindings per spec item 6, each with serde round-trip unit tests using captured/documented JSON fixtures.
4. Author error.rs per spec item 7.
5. Implement client.rs spawn path: build the identity-locked launch plan (reusing the npm-shim resolution on Windows; direct native executable on all platforms), spawn via the MT-004 stdio infra, register with the MT-005 supervisor.
6. Implement the read loop: line-split with cap, classify response vs notification vs server-request, correlate/dispatch per spec items 3-4.
7. Implement the initialize handshake per spec item 5 with timeout.
8. Implement health.rs per spec item 8 and shutdown per spec item 9.
9. Unit-test correlation, dispatch, handshake, timeout, pending-drain-on-exit, and notification overflow against an in-process fake transport (duplex pipe feeding scripted JSONL) - the fake exercises the REAL client code; it is not a mock of the client.
10. Add one live smoke test (feature/env-gated) that spawns the real `codex app-server` when the CLI is installed and authenticated; when absent, emit the typed blocker NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF - never silently skip.
11. Run proof targets; record measured outputs.
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/official_cli_bridge.rs (visibility widening of existing npm-shim resolution/identity helpers only; no exec-lane behavior change)
src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml (only if a new dev-dependency for duplex-pipe testing is required)
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (no GUI work in this MT)
acceptance_criteria: codex_app_server module compiles inside handshake_core with client.rs, protocol.rs, error.rs, health.rs and is registered in cloud/mod.rs.

On Windows the spawn path resolves codex.cmd through the SAME identity-verified npm-shim resolution used by the exec lane (manifest name @openai/codex, bin.codex == bin/codex.js) and executes the pinned native image directly; a tampered shim is rejected with a typed ShimIdentity error (negative test).
Request/response correlation: concurrent in-flight requests resolve to the correct callers (test with >= 8 interleaved requests over the fake transport).
Child-exit drain: when the transport closes with pending requests, every pending caller receives CodexAppServerError::ChannelClosed within the deadline; none hang (test).
Notification dispatch: thread/turn/item notifications reach subscribers in arrival order; overflow increments a dropped-count instead of blocking the read loop (test).
Server-to-client requests (approval shapes) with no registered handler receive a typed JSON-RPC error response; the id is never dropped (test).
Initialize handshake completes before any other method is sent; calling another method pre-handshake returns a typed error (test); handshake timeout yields CodexAppServerError::Handshake (test).
Unterminated-line hard cap enforced: an over-cap line terminates the transport with a typed error instead of unbounded buffering (test).
health() returns the typed snapshot fields named in the spec and flips alive=false after child exit (test).
Shutdown/drop leaves no orphan child process (test asserts child reaped; HBR-QUIET-003 ownership metadata recorded via the MT-005 supervisor seam).
All protocol bindings round-trip serde on documented fixtures including unknown-variant tolerance (test).
Live spawn smoke test passes against an installed authenticated codex CLI, OR the typed blocker NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF is recorded; silent skip is prohibited.
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake_core model_runtime::cloud::official_cli_bridge -- --nocapture  # exec-lane regression: visibility widening changed no behavior
HSK_CODEX_LIVE=1 cargo test -p handshake_core codex_app_server_live_spawn -- --nocapture --ignored  # live smoke; absent CLI/login => typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF record, never silent skip
expected_tests: codex_app_server_live_spawn (live-gated; typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF when CLI/login absent)
implementation_notes: Transport decision is pre-made: stdio JSONL (stable, default). The experimental WebSocket transport and Unix-socket transport are OUT OF SCOPE (REJECTED for this WP); do not add config knobs for them.

The exec lane (codex exec --json) is a DIFFERENT process shape parsed by agent_activity.rs parse_codex_line (fn at line 284; dispatch at line 131); do not route app-server frames through it. MT-045 owns event recording; this MT only exposes the typed notification stream.
The correlation map must never be held across an .await while dispatching; lock, remove the sender, unlock, then send.

Bindings are hand-authored on purpose (small verified surface). `codex app-server generate-json-schema` output is the source of truth; MT-047 checks drift in CI. Do not vendor the generated schema as runtime code.
Per HBR-INT-008 any new id minted for internal correlation entities uses Uuid::now_v7 where a Uuid is used; the JSON-RPC wire id stays a plain u64.
Keep the public API lane-shaped for MT-042/043/044: expose request(method, params) -> typed result, subscribe_events(), register_server_request_handler(), health(), shutdown().

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless backend transport MT: no operator-visible surface changed; visual verification = TraceProjection per HBR-VIS-004.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal transport core with no operator-usable behavior yet; the Codex persistent-lane UserManual entry is owned by MT-043/MT-044/MT-046 which wire operator-meaningful capabilities. If the UserManual artifact is absent in the implementation worktree, record DEFERRED-with-reason per HBR-MAN-001.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Transport lifecycle (spawn/handshake/exit) emits FR business events via the lane observability seam; full event mapping is MT-045.
internal_diagnostics wiring recorded as DEFERRED-with-reason if the tool is not present in the implementation worktree at claim time; never silently skipped.
External watcher registration for app-server child liveness deferred to the MT-005 supervisor integration; recorded, never silently skipped.

risk_if_missed: No persistent Codex lane exists: no mid-turn steering, no approvals bridge, no resume/fork; the entire CX group (MT-042..047) is blocked and Codex remains one-shot-only.

risks: RISK-1: Shim-identity bypass - spawning codex.cmd via cmd.exe (or skipping manifest verification) lets a tampered shim run arbitrary code inside the runtime process tree.
RISK-2: Correlation leak/hang - a child crash with pending requests leaves callers awaiting forever, freezing session lanes.
RISK-3: Unbounded buffering - a malformed or hostile server emitting a never-terminated line or a notification flood balloons memory.
RISK-4: Handshake deadlock - blocking synchronous read during initialize wedges the adapter when the server writes nothing.
RISK-5: Orphan processes - app-server children outlive sessions/tests, violating process-ownership discipline.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Reuse resolve_codex_npm_shim + launch-plan identity locks (official_cli_bridge.rs 1263, 1223-1240); execute the pinned native image directly; negative test proves a tampered shim is rejected typed.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Monotonic ids + drain-all-pending-with-ChannelClosed on transport end; test asserts no hung future.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Reuse the cli_bridge_runtime line hard cap; bounded notification channels with dropped-count; tests for both.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Fully async read loop + bounded handshake timeout returning typed Handshake error; test.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Supervisor registration with ownership metadata + kill-on-drop + graceful shutdown deadline; test asserts child reaped (HBR-QUIET-003).
